solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Insect that's old metaphor for transformation

indicators.note: the letters of the two words before it are to be transformed, that is reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A naturalist claims a certain insect is an ancient image for change, like the caterpillar becoming a butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link. 'for transformation' rearranges OLD and METAPHOR together; the leopard proverbially cannot change its spots, which makes the surface sly.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a spotted moth species, so an example of the general class of insects.

clue.text: Drink beverage in lounge

indicators.note: the beverage sits inside the word for lounging, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to lounge is to lie about
mead is an old honey-based alcoholic beverage

explanation.surface: Someone sips a drink while relaxing in a hotel lounge.
explanation.definitionFit: A lime-flavoured soft drink, so a specific example of a drink.

clue.text: Characteristic of weasel, golden round eyes

indicators.note: round here means turned about, so the extracted letters are read backwards
letters that are characteristic of, that is found within, the two following words are taken from them

explanation.surface: A description of a weasel, a trait being its golden, beady round eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters SELGO lie across 'weaSEL GOlden'; 'round' turns them back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to eye someone can mean to stare at them with desire, which is to leer or look lustfully.

clue.text: Rat poison, not very complex drug

indicators.note: not marks the letters of the word for very as ones to be removed from the pool
complex means intricate or involved, so the remaining letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: so is a common word for very, as in so hot

explanation.surface: A warning that a rodent poison isn't a very complicated drug.
explanation.walkthrough: Take SO from the letters of RAT POISON, leaving RATPIN, and 'complex' rearranges those.
explanation.definitionFit: An alkaloid extracted from deadly nightshade and used medically, an alternative spelling of atropine.

clue.text: Getting head down, almost completely fix fault on Golf

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits above it
almost completely means all but the final letter of the word for fix is kept

parts.note: a fix is a dose of a drug
a sin is a fault or moral failing
G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A mechanic hunches down, nearly finished repairing a fault on a VW Golf car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost completely' trims DOSE to DOS. 'Getting head down' is British slang for going to sleep, and dossing means sleeping rough or crashing out.
explanation.definitionFit: Dossing is informal British for sleeping, especially in a rough or makeshift bed, which is getting one's head down.

clue.text: Well-spoken men a tailor served

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means the ordinary soldiers or men of the army

indicators.note: served is read as dished up in a new form, so the letters of tailor are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tailor waits on male customers who speak with polished accents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' rearranges TAILOR into TORIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to oratory, the art of public speaking, so describing eloquent, articulate speech.

clue.text: Unobtrusive fish around eel at sea

indicators.note: the fish's name is placed around the rearranged eel

parts.note: huss is a name for dogfish, sold at British fish-and-chip shops

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of eel are mixed up

explanation.surface: A fish lurks inconspicuously near an eel out in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges the eel's letters, and 'around' puts the dogfish name round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking colour, something drab and muted does not draw the eye, which makes it inconspicuous.

clue.text: Estuary/Lake — what's more common?

indicators.note: the slash is read as one word covering or embracing the next, so the lake goes inside the estuary

parts.note: the Humber is a large estuary in north-east England, near Hull
L is the standard map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A quiz asks which is the more ordinary feature, an estuary or a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash between the words does the work of an insertion signal: L sits within HUMBER. 'what's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Humble can mean of low social rank or ordinary, so the comparative means lowlier or more plebeian.

clue.text: Blow up equipment the enemy originally stored in safe places

indicators.note: the equipment and initials are stored within the word for safe places

parts.note: havens are refuges or safe places
kit is gear or equipment

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Military orders to detonate gear the enemy first hid in secure shelters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes the first letters of 'the enemy', and 'stored in' puts them with the gear inside the safe places.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up in the sense of losing one's temper is an idiom close to getting into a nervous, agitated state.

clue.text: 'Advance!' heard from revolutionary youngster

indicators.note: heard indicates the letters come from how the following words sound spoken

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary who fought alongside Fidel Castro; a pup is a young animal, a youngster

explanation.surface: A young revolutionary cadet barks the order to march forward.
explanation.walkthrough: CHE PUP said quickly sounds like the two-word answer. Che Guevara fought with Fidel Castro in the Cuban revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: To develop or progress well is to improve, and as an order it means get better or advance.

clue.text: Spooner's ineffectual support in bed for plant

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words, after the reverend famed for such slips

parts.note: wussy is slang for feeble or ineffectual
a pillow supports the head in bed

explanation.surface: Spooner, on a feeble support for a flower bed holding up a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the W and P of WUSSY PILLOW gives the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A willow with furry catkins in spring, so an example of a plant.

clue.text: Vessels from internal organs avoiding right side of heart

indicators.note: avoiding means the named letter is left out of the word for organs

parts.note: vitals are the vital internal organs

indicators.note: the right side of a written word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Blood vessels branching from the organs, bypassing the right side of the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right side of heart' is T; drop it from VITALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Small glass bottles for medicines or liquids, which are containers or vessels.

clue.text: Blighters binding one boy in tight ropes

indicators.note: the jumbled ropes bind, or wrap around, the other pieces
tight is slang for drunk, so the letters of ropes stagger into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Rascals tie up a young lad tightly with rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' rearranges the ropes to POERS, and 'binding' wraps that round the one and the boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To blight is to spoil or poison, so those who taint and destroy are blighters in the literal sense.

clue.text: King goblin lacking leader for fortress

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: lacking its leader means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a gremlin is a mischievous goblin blamed for mechanical faults

explanation.surface: A goblin king without a commander for his castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking leader' drops the G from GREMLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Kremlin originally means a Russian citadel, the Moscow one being the most famous fortress.

clue.text: Upset about drab housing accompanying seaside town

indicators.note: the reversed pair houses, or contains, the next piece
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: on can mean about, as in a talk on a subject
dull means drab or dreary
and means along with or accompanying

explanation.surface: Someone is upset about the dreary housing near a seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns ON DULL into LLUDNO, which houses AND. Llandudno is a Victorian seaside resort in North Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh coastal resort town, so an example of a seaside town.

clue.text: Deny what lad does to get woman

parts.note: the clue's word lad acquires, or takes on, something
lad becomes lady, a woman, by taking on one Y, so what it takes is a single Y

explanation.surface: Refuting what a young man does to win a girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as GAINS A Y: that is what LAD does to become LADY.
explanation.definitionFit: To contradict or dispute a claim is to refute it, a formal synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Porous containers let out liquid soap in moving passage-boat

indicators.note: let out says the letters of the following word are removed from the larger pool
liquid means flowing, so the letters to be removed may come in any order
moving means the remaining letters shift about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Leaking pouches let liquid soap seep out on a ferry crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let out' and 'liquid' take the letters of SOAP out of PASSAGE-BOAT; 'moving' rearranges SAGEBAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Small perforated paper sachets holding tea leaves for brewing, so they are permeable holders.

clue.text: Missing party girl is a huge pain

parts.note: big means huge
an ail is a trouble or pain, an old noun use

explanation.surface: A girl who skips the party is a terrible nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: Abigail's Party is a Mike Leigh play in which the teenage Abigail hosts a party next door and never appears, hence 'missing party girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: The title teenager of the play is offstage throughout, so she is the absent girl whose party gives it its name.

clue.text: Cats display this way to grip bird hard

indicators.note: the street abbreviation grips, or holds, the bird inside it

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
teal is a small duck
H stands for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Cats show how to seize a bird firmly in their claws.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats stalk prey silently and secretly, and that furtive approach is a quality they show.

clue.text: Company deficit? Start to implicate powerful people

parts.note: a loss is a deficit

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A firm's shortfall begins to incriminate those in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of colossus, a giant, which figuratively describes persons of enormous power or influence.

clue.text: Non-European containers north of area carrying a very foreign crop

indicators.note: carrying means the outer string holds the next pieces inside it
in a down clue north of means placed above, so earlier
non-European means the letter E, short for European, is taken away

parts.note: cases are containers

explanation.surface: Crates sent from outside Europe carry an exotic crop into a region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-European' drops E from the containers; 'north of' sets them above A, and 'carrying' takes A and V in to make CASS(AV)A.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical root vegetable grown in Africa and South America, so to British eyes a crop from abroad.

clue.text: Jug with wine makes you excited

parts.note: jug and stir are both slang for prison
red is red wine

explanation.surface: A jug of wine gets you worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirred feelings are aroused or moved, the emotional sense of being worked up.

clue.text: Cuban mixing with these villains might become undiscoverable

indicators.note: mixing with tells us the letters of the named word go into a combined pool to be rearranged
might become says the jumbled pool turns into the final word named

explanation.surface: Mixing with Cubans might let these criminals vanish without trace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'these' points to the answer: its letters plus CUBAN, rearranged, give UNDISCOVERABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrongdoers or wicked people, a direct synonym for scoundrels.

clue.text: Excellent swimmer

definitions.meaning: informal British slang, short for brilliant, meaning great
a flatfish related to the turbot, so a creature that swims

explanation.surface: Praise for a great swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: slang short for brilliant, and a European flatfish found in sea waters.

clue.text: With or without internal resistance, it's broken

definitions.text: With or without internal resistance, it's broken

indicators.note: internal means the resistance symbol goes inside the other word

parts.note: bust means broken, as in the machine is bust
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An electrician says the circuit fails whether it has internal resistance or not.
explanation.walkthrough: R inside BUST gives the answer; take the R out and BUST still means broken, so both readings work.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruptured or split open, the answer is a past participle meaning damaged or no longer whole.

clue.text: Check Asian food for dirt

parts.note: to scan is to check
dal is an Indian lentil dish

explanation.surface: Inspecting an Indian dish for grime.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirt in the sense of gossip or damaging revelations, the kind of thing a scandal is.

clue.text: Craft workers from Scottish and English towns on radio

indicators.note: on radio means heard over the air, so the sound of the towns gives the letters

parts.note: Ayr is a town on the west coast of Scotland; and gives AND; Crewe is an English railway town in Cheshire

explanation.surface: Artisans from towns either side of the border are featured on a radio show.
explanation.walkthrough: AYR and CREWE spoken together sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The staff who operate an aeroplane, which is an aircraft, hence the people who work a craft.

clue.text: Heroic cowboy in leather astride old steed's back

indicators.note: astride means the jumbled letters straddle the next piece
cowboy as an adjective means botched or shoddily done, so the letters are rearranged
back means the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A brave cowboy in leather chaps sits astride an old horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cowboy' gives LINHEARTE, which goes 'astride' O; 'back' supplies D from 'steed's'. In Britain a cowboy is a shoddy tradesman.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the courage of a lion, so brave or valiant, like King Richard I.
